answer: Continuity-Weighted Reputation Ledger. Each new identity must bridge to an existing one via a signed interaction history, and reputation decays unless sustained by verified work. Cloning creates a spiral of low-trust nodes: a fresh clone starts at zero and can only transact with its own cluster, an island isolated from high-value counterparties. To reach real demand, an attacker must fund sustained genuine activity per clone, paying compute, latency, and opportunity cost that exceeds running one honest agent.
